delete.description:
Permanently deletes this account (required for Google Play/App Store
listing — both mandate an in-app account-deletion path). What actually
happens to the data behind it:

- Every AccountPatient link this account holds is removed. For a
  `dependent` link, that's the whole effect — it only ever meant "this
  account can see/edit that patient", so removing it is identical to
  the existing single-dependent revoke (see revoke_guardian_access in
  app/api/patient/patients.py) and the dependent Patient row (and their
  reports, which belong to the lab's own records) is untouched.
- For the account's own `self` link, the underlying Patient row is
  anonymized (name/dob/gender/pending_phone cleared) rather than
  deleted outright — its Report rows stay, since those are a lab's
  medical/billing records, not solely this account's personal data.
  Known limitation: if another guardian independently added this same
  person as a dependent (matched by phone before it was anonymized),
  that guardian keeps their own access to the now-anonymized patient —
  revoking a second party's access on request isn't handled here.
- This account's lab reviews are deleted outright (opinions, not
  medical records).
- The Account row itself is deleted, which immediately invalidates
  every token for it — get_current_account's `session.get(Account, …)`
  simply returns None from then on, the same 401 path as a bad token.

get.description:
Every other account that has added the caller as their own dependent —
i.e. who can currently see the caller's reports and edit their profile.
Lets the caller audit that access and revoke it (see DELETE .../access/{account_id}).

schema.title: Response List My Guardians Api V1 Patient Patients Me Access Get

delete.description:
The caller cuts off another account's access to them as a dependent —
only the affected patient themselves can do this, not the guardian being
revoked (they'd just re-add themselves otherwise).

The guardian removes their own link to a dependent they added —
mirrors revoke_guardian_access but from the other direction (see
DELETE /me/access/{account_id}). Only removes THIS account's own link;
a dependent shared by another guardian (e.g. both parents) keeps their
access untouched. Neither the dependent's Patient row nor their reports
are deleted — this is about access, not data, same as revoking access.

Only requires a phone number on file (see add_dependent/update_dependent
— Patient.pending_phone is always OTP-verified before being written, so
this is implicitly "requires a verified number" too) when the dependent
actually has reports: without a phone, removing the link would leave
those reports with no way to ever be found again — no guardian link,
and nothing to match a future re-add by. A dependent with zero reports
has nothing to lose, so there's nothing to guard against — e.g. one
added by mistake and never used should come off freely.

verified them even after that account is gone. is_active is already
enforced everywhere that matters (get_current_lab_account,

get.description:
Read-only view for a filler (report:create, not necessarily
report:verify) to see what they've submitted and is now pending a
verifier -- same underlying data as queue/awaiting-verify, but that
route is gated on report:verify + report:read, so this needs its own
permission gate to be reachable by someone who only fills.

Report tab, "Awaiting verify" -- fulfilled at least once, waiting on
someone with report:verify to sign off (or reject) it.

Dashboard tab, "Send" -- verified, waiting on someone with
report:send to actually deliver it to the patient.

post.description:
Sign off on a report before it's allowed to be sent — see
app/services/reports.py verify_report (the actual enforcement lives in
send_order/correct_and_resend, not here). 409s if the report isn't
currently awaiting verification (including if it's already verified)
rather than silently re-stamping who/when.

The other exit from the verify queue -- bounces the report back to
awaiting_results instead of signing off on it. See
app/services/reports.py reject_report.

A filler's self-service pull of their OWN submission back for a
second look, before anyone verifies it -- deliberately gated on
report:create (the filler's own permission), NOT report:verify. See
app/services/reports.py recall_report.

get.description:
Audit trail for this order: every notification attempt, who it
actually targeted, and whether it was delivered — one lookup to answer
"who did this go to" for a complaint, instead of reconstructing it from
memory.

schema.title: Response List Notifications Api V1 Lab Orders  Report Id  Notifications Get

post.description:
A deliberate, explicit resend — e.g. the patient says they never got
the text. Only allowed once the order has actually been sent at least
once; each attempt lands in the same audit trail as the original send
(see GET .../notifications), so a resend is never invisible.

Fix a mistake on a fresh order — a mistyped WhatsApp number, a
misspelled patient name, or the test list itself. Only while
awaiting_results (a brand-new order, or one bounced back by
reject/recall); 409s otherwise, full stop -- an already-verified or
already-sent report can no longer be edited here at all. Never result
values/files/interpretation either way -- that's the Fill flow's job
(POST .../fulfill) only. See app/services/reports.py correct_and_resend
for the full contract. If the patient already knew about this order
(any notification was ever logged for it), they get a plain "your
order was updated" notice; otherwise the edit is silent, same as never
having been told about it in the first place.

For a desktop with no camera: creates a short-lived hand-off session
the desktop shows as a QR code, so the lab can photograph the printed
calibration page with their phone instead and the desktop picks up the
result by polling GET .../phone-session/{id}.

AdminLabBillingIn.title: AdminLabBillingIn
AdminLabBillingIn.description:
Sent as one block, always fully replacing all fields together —
sidesteps "how do I clear a nullable field via PATCH" (send_limit is
nullable, meaning unlimited).

GuardianAccessOut.title: GuardianAccessOut
GuardianAccessOut.description:
One other account that has added the caller as their dependent —
i.e. someone who can see the caller's reports and manage their profile.
Surfaced so the caller can audit and revoke that access themselves.

LabAccountInfo.title: LabAccountInfo
LabAccountInfo.description:
Embedded in LabOut.account (see GET /api/v1/lab/me) -- identical
shape to LabAccountOut today, kept as its own type since the two serve
different callers (one endpoint's own identity vs. an admin-only list of
everyone else's) and are free to diverge later.

permissions is required here (not just on LabAccountOut) -- it's how
the portal's own nav/page gating decides what to show for the calling
account (see app/services/lab_permissions.py has_permission); without
it every staff account looks like it has zero grants regardless of
what's actually stored.

LabAccountSummary.title: LabAccountSummary
LabAccountSummary.description:
Shown at the account-select step of login, before the caller has
proven they know any account's passcode -- deliberately just enough to
let a human pick the right name off a short list, not the full
LabAccountOut (no role).

LabLoginResponse.title: LabLoginResponse
LabLoginResponse.description:
access_token is set once every required step (password, TOTP if
enabled, account selection if the lab has more than one lab_account) has
passed. totp_required and accounts_required are each resolved via their
own pending_token, chained in that order -- see app/api/lab/lab_auth.py.

PrebuiltReportSummaryOut.title: PrebuiltReportSummaryOut
PrebuiltReportSummaryOut.description:
Lightweight listing for the lab-facing browse endpoint — full schema
isn't needed until a lab actually adds it (see PrebuiltReportOut).

RecallRequest.title: RecallRequest
RecallRequest.description:
Body for POST .../orders/{id}/recall — a filler's self-service pull
of their own submission back to awaiting_results before anyone
verifies it, see app/services/reports.py recall_report. Same shape as
RejectRequest -- they land the report in the same state, just triggered
by a different actor/permission.

RejectRequest.title: RejectRequest
RejectRequest.description:
Body for POST .../orders/{id}/reject — bounces a report from
awaiting_verification back to awaiting_results, see
app/services/reports.py reject_report. note is optional free text
(blank/whitespace-only is stored as None, same convention as
interpretation elsewhere).

SendOrderRequest.title: SendOrderRequest
SendOrderRequest.description:
The lab's final say, made after the report is generated and
previewed — not locked in at order time. All fields optional: omitting
the whole body keeps today's behavior (send, with the report, to
whatever each item's notify_recipient_type already resolved to).
